title: fix(react,app-shell): a nav entry and a page element bound to the same API read make one request per open (objectui#13323)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuBkYnqatuvYPHy911yUqv1k)_

Fixes #13323

Refs: objectstack-ai/cloud#3103 (the maintainer's ask; cloud's `console-boots` reads the result on the next cloud pin PR)

- [x] Adds no product-specific widget, dialog, hook or string (see AGENTS.md › Product-neutral renderer). `ElementApiOpenScope` and `ConsoleElementApiOpen` are named for what they do; no product URL or name appears outside tests.

Clause-②: yes (new exports from `@object-ui/react`, reached through its existing `export *` of `element-data-source/useElementApiDataSource.js`: `ElementApiOpenScope`, `useElementApiOpen`, the `ElementApiOpen` type, and an optional third parameter on `readElementApi`. Nothing new is exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s entry: `ConsoleElementApiOpen` is an internal module.)

## What was wrong

A nav entry declaring an API `dataSource` and a page element bound to the same read made two `GET`s on one console open. The nav gate (`useNavMemberGates` → `readElementApi`) read first. The page element (`useElementApiDataSource` → `readElementApi`) read about 300 ms later. `readElementApi` shared a request only while it was in flight (`.finally(() => IN_FLIGHT.delete(url))`). Once the nav read had settled, the element's read went to the network again. Cloud measured `GET /api/v1/cloud/home x2` on `page/welcome`, and `page/pricing` went over its budget (23 calls against 22).

## The change

- **`@object-ui/react`**: `ElementApiOpenScope({ open, children })` keeps the reads asked under the `open` name it is given, in a map the scope owns. `readElementApi(url, doFetch, open?)` hands back a read that the same open already asked for, whether settled or pending, and sends no request. Otherwise it behaves as before (the in-flight share, then a new request) and records the read under the open. It does not hand out:
  - **a failed read.** It is removed when it rejects, so the next reader asks again.
  - **a read from another open.** Its name differs, it is never returned, and it is pruned at the next keep.
  - **anything read before a declared data change.** The scope subscribes to `subscribeDataChanges` and clears its reads on any `notifyDataChanged`. An endpoint names no object, so every change counts. A read after an action asks the server.
- **No read is moved in time.** `useElementApiDataSource` and `useNavEntryData` still ask exactly when they asked before. Their effects leave `open` out of the deps on purpose (commented, with an `exhaustive-deps` disable). A change of open never triggers a read on its own. The open only decides whether a read the binding already asked for reaches the network. Effects key on the scope's `reads` map (state-owned) and on the `open` string, never on the context value's identity (AGENTS.md #10).
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`**: `ConnectedShellInner` mounts `ConsoleElementApiOpen` inside the `MetadataProvider key={language}` remount, so a language switch starts over. The component names one open per visit of a history entry:
  - **`PUSH` and `POP` start a new open.** Following a link or a nav entry, or going Back or Forward, reads again. No answer outlives the visit it was read in, not even on an entry visited before. The name is the entry's key plus a count of the opens the scope has seen, because `POP` restores an entry's original key (seat review, patch round 1).
  - **`REPLACE` stays in the open.** The app root's landing replaces `/apps/:appName` with its first entry once the nav reads have answered (`<Navigate to={landing} replace />`). That is the welcome / pricing path cloud measures, and the page it lands on is the same visit. The other replaces in the console rewrite the page they are on: a URL-state update such as search params, or a legacy-address redirect to the page that address names. The answer they keep was read during this same visit. It is never another page's, because any move to another page through a link, a nav entry or history is a `PUSH` or `POP`.
  - The name is derived during render with React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern. No reader below ever runs under the previous open's name on a new entry, whatever the effect order. With no router, the component renders its children bare: nothing is kept, as before.
- **File surface:** `ConsoleShell.tsx` and the new internal `ConsoleElementApiOpen.tsx` lie outside the claim's first file surface (`apps/console/src/**` was named for the wiring). The seat approved this before the push, and the card carries the surface revision.
- **Docs:** `content/docs/guide/data-source.md` (the old "Nothing is cached" paragraph is replaced by the one-open rule), the `@object-ui/react` README (`useElementApiDataSource` section) and the `@object-ui/app-shell` README (product blocks). **Changeset:** `@object-ui/react` minor (new export), `@object-ui/app-shell` patch. No `major`.

## Verification

Heads `c417da7` and `e06ab07` (patch round 1) were run locally. Each run below has its result.

- **Card acceptance, one request per open:** `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/navEntryReadReuse-13323.test.tsx`. It mounts the real `ConsoleElementApiOpen`, `ExpressionProvider`, `MePermissionsProvider`, `useNavMemberGates` and `SchemaRenderer`, with a stubbed host `apiFetch`. The page element mounts only after the nav read has SETTLED, which is the case in-flight sharing misses.
  - (a) one open: 1 call.
  - (b) the app root, then a `replace` to the page (the landing): 1 call.
  - (c) a `PUSH` to another page, then Back: 2, then 3 calls, each element drawing that open's answer.
  - (c') a page that reads U, a `PUSH` to a page that reads nothing, then Back: 2 calls, with the newer answer drawn. Added in patch round 1. It was red on `c417da7` (`expected '1' to be '5'`, the first visit's answer handed back under the restored key) and is green on `e06ab07`.
  - (d) `notifyDataChanged` between the nav read and the element: 2 calls, and the element draws the newer answer.
  - (e) a 500 nav read: the entry stays hidden, as objectui#13029 requires, and the element asks again: 2 calls.
  - (f) control with no scope: 2 calls, the defect as it was.
  - Result: 7/7 passed on `e06ab07`.
- **The public export alone:** `packages/react/src/element-data-source/__tests__/elementApiOpenScope-13323.test.tsx`. Same open: 1 call. Another open name: 2. No scope: 2. Result: 3/3 passed.
- **Ablations,** each run on the working tree and restored from a byte copy, with zero ablation markers left (`grep -c` 0 after each):
  - The reuse line removed from `readElementApi` (the card's "without the reuse"): (a), (b) and (c) fail with `expected 2 to be 1`.
  - The open-name check removed (reuse across opens): (c) fails with `expected '1' to be '2'`, a stale answer on the new open.
  - The data-change clear and the failure removal both removed: (d) fails with `expected '1' to be '4'`, and (e) fails.
  - `REPLACE` treated as a new open: (b) fails with `expected 2 to be 1`. Re-run on `e06ab07` with the same result.
  - The per-visit count removed, so the name is the entry key alone (the `c417da7` code): (c') fails with `expected '1' to be '5'`.
- **Suites:** `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/ packages/app-shell/ apps/console/`, run under `os-verify-lock.sh` (VERDICT command-exit 0): 2038 files passed and 1 skipped; 19447 tests passed and 9 skipped. The existing nav-binding pins (`navEntryDataSource-13029`, `AppContent.landingWaitsReads-13097`) and `ConnectedShell.sessionGate` are part of that run, and their requests are unchanged. On `e06ab07`, the two new test files and `packages/react/src/element-data-source/` passed 126/126, and the app-shell type-check passed 30/30.
- **Type-check:** `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/app-shell --filter=@object-ui/react` with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`: 31/31 tasks. At the default heap, app-shell's `tsc` ran out of memory (exit 134), so this is a heap limit, not a type error.
- **ESLint** on every changed source and test file: 0 errors. The warnings in `ConsoleShell.tsx` and `useNavMemberGates.ts` are pre-existing and sit on lines this PR does not touch. `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-element-data-source-declaration` and `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new) all pass.
- **The consumer reading** (the card's last acceptance note) belongs on the cloud pin PR that carries this fix. Cloud's `console-boots` should show `page/welcome` with no duplicate URL and `page/pricing` within 22, with the budget unmoved. It does not gate this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- None out of scope. The page element still does not re-read on its own after an action: it subscribes to no invalidation bus, which is pre-existing behaviour and outside this card. What changed is that no read asked after a write is answered from before it.
